title: Metal CPU-accessible placement heaps are attempted on Intel macOS without a supported strategy
body:
Source/native-contract finding on main fc22df0; no Intel Mac runtime was available to validate a replacement.

The allocator constructs CPU-accessible Shared placement-heap descriptors for CpuToGpu/GpuToCpu on every device. Apple's MTLHeapDescriptor.storageMode documentation permits only Private heaps on macOS devices without Apple silicon. Thus CPU-visible buffer allocation on those devices requests an unsupported heap rather than selecting a supported committed/managed resource strategy or explicitly rejecting the unsupported configuration. The resulting nil can be reported as OutOfMemory even though the descriptor/platform combination is unsupported.

Suggested runtime reproduction on an Intel Mac: allocate a small CpuToGpu buffer using AllocationCreateDesc::buffer, enable Metal API validation, and inspect newHeapWithDescriptor and the returned error. Expected behavior needs an explicit backend support decision: supported non-heap CPU-visible allocations, or a clear platform/feature error. Retrying smaller Shared heaps cannot resolve an unsupported storage mode.

[Apple heap storage-mode contract](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlheapdescriptor/storagemode). This is distinct from the Shared-texture wildcard routing issue https://github.com/Traverse-Research/gpu-allocator/issues/330. #323 preserves the existing resource model and has only Apple cross-compilation, not Apple runtime validation.

Agent-assisted investigation and report. Evidence: https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/allocator-reconciliation-20261128
